competition: DrivenData #306 — DOE Geologic Enhanced Mapping System (GEMS) Prize
hypothesis: Unmapped geothermal-indicative faults in NW Great Basin follow two distinct geological regimes: (A) Mode-II/III elastic fracture-process-zone continuations, fracture-arrest stress shadows, and collinear/en-echelon relay bridges extending from known USGS/INGENIOUS fault tips, and (B) buried greenfield range-front and piedmont structures characterized by high 3D crustal slip/dilation tendency (Ts, Td), hanging-wall-pulled gravity/magnetic basement steps, 1m LiDAR scarp asymmetry, and convective hydrothermal upflow / boiling-zone K/Th alteration anomalies.
mechanism: Two-Regime spatially blocked 4-quadrant out-of-fold LightGBM posterior fusing 34 strictly label-free multi-physics channels (1m 3DEP LiDAR scarps, 100m DEM breaklines + shoreline mimic rejection, 2.5-3.0 px up-dip potential-field worms, USGS 3D crustal Cauchy Ts/Td stress at sigma=25 km, GDR 1391 geothermometers, USGS convective heat-flow residuals, shallow 3D Euler contacts, GeoDAWN K/Th & demag) with 13 fold-strict directed topology channels trained via nested self-supervised hide-and-recover, allocated into sparse binary {0.0, 1.0} off-catalogue dots (d_cat > 200 m) via exact 6-shell discrete Choquet-survival Minoux-Dinkelbach fractional programming.
named_non_fault_mimic: Pleistocene Lake Lahontan (~1332 m) & Lake Bonneville (~1463/1552 m) wave-cut paleoshoreline benches, Miocene basalt mesa rims, symmetric fluvial canyon risers, and un-slipped pluton contacts — suppressed explicitly by shoreline_mimic_penalty (contour breakline lacking subsurface gravity/basement offset), 1m LiDAR scarp asymmetry (lid_tect_ratio), and 3D Cauchy slip/dilation tendency (Ts * Td).
